subject: general
question: Which of the following is an alarming effect of thermal pollution in water bodies?

options.text: The amount of dissolved oxygen decreased significantly
The random changes in pH values

solution:
The correct answer is __**The amount of dissolved oxygen decreased significantly**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Thermal pollution increases the temperature of water bodies, which reduces the solubility of oxygen in water.
 
• Lower levels of dissolved oxygen negatively impact aquatic organisms, disrupting their respiration and survival mechanisms.
 
• Decreased dissolved oxygen can lead to hypoxic conditions, causing mass deaths of fish and other aquatic life.
 
• Warm water also accelerates the metabolic rates of aquatic organisms, increasing their oxygen demand while simultaneously reducing oxygen availability.
 
• Thermal pollution is often caused by industrial discharges, such as cooling water from power plants, or urban runoff that raises water temperatures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thermal Pollution:**

 
 
• Thermal pollution occurs when industries discharge heated water or effluents into natural water bodies, altering the temperature balance.
 
• It negatively impacts aquatic ecosystems by disrupting breeding patterns, migration cycles, and biodiversity.
 
• Sources include power plants, manufacturing industries, deforestation, and urban runoff.
 
 
 
• **Dissolved Oxygen (DO):**
 
 
• Dissolved oxygen refers to the amount of oxygen present in water, essential for the survival of aquatic organisms.
 
• DO levels are inversely proportional to water temperature – higher temperatures reduce oxygen solubility.
 
• Low DO levels can lead to hypoxic conditions, affecting aquatic biodiversity and ecosystem health.
 
 
 
• **Hypoxia:**
 
 
• Hypoxia refers to oxygen deficiency in water, often caused by thermal pollution or organic matter decomposition.
 
• It can result in dead zones where aquatic life struggles to survive, such as areas in the Gulf of Mexico.
 
• Hypoxia disrupts food chains and aquatic ecosystems, leading to significant ecological damage.
 
 
 
• **Control Measures:**
 
 
• Cooling ponds, cooling towers, and heat exchangers can be used to minimize thermal pollution.
 
• Planting vegetation along water bodies helps reduce temperature fluctuations and runoff impacts.
 
• Regulating industrial discharges through environmental laws ensures better temperature management in water bodies.
